memo.intro: First-look memo as of 2026-11-01. Public data only. Every factual sentence links to its source; a separate verifier removed unsupported claims.

sentences.text: The sources show two GitHub repositories under the cvg organization: cvg/VIGS-SLAM and cvg/vidmap.
sentences.note: Both repos are under cvg, but the sources do not say they are the only evidence or that they are public.

sentences.text: VIGS-SLAM is described as a visual inertial Gaussian splatting SLAM project accepted at ECCV'26, with topics including robotics and slam.
sentences.note: Description says [ECCV'26] Visual Inertial Gaussian Splatting SLAM; topics include robotics and slam.

sentences.text: vidmap is described as video-based structure-from-motion work for ECCV 2026.
As of 2026-11-02, vidmap had 487 stars and 39 forks, and VIGS-SLAM had 115 stars and 11 forks.
The evidence shows research code releases.
It does not show a company, a product, customers, or funding.
The evidence does not identify the cvg team or any company founders.
The arXiv paper for VidMap lists three authors: Zador Pataki, Paul-Edouard Sarlin, and Marc Pollefeys.
The evidence does not say whether these authors are founders of a venture or how they relate to cvg beyond the paper and repository.
The VidMap abstract says it combines the sequential constraints of SLAM with the global optimization of offline SfM to reconstruct long, uncalibrated videos at metric scale.
sentences.note: Abstract states combining SLAM sequential constraints with offline SfM global optimization for metric reconstruction of long uncalibrated videos.

sentences.text: The abstract says it uses recent advances in wide-baseline dense image matching.
sentences.note: Abstract says it leverages recent advances in wide-baseline dense image matching.

sentences.text: The abstract frames the goal as recovering camera calibration and metric poses for unconstrained video.
sentences.note: Abstract opens with recovering calibration and metric poses for unconstrained video.

sentences.text: What looks novel is the hybrid framing: using temporal order as a constraint while still optimizing globally, without known calibration.
What is hard is robustness across arbitrary video, including symmetric scenes, extreme motion, and long sequences, while keeping metric scale correct.
VIGS-SLAM combines visual and inertial input with Gaussian splatting for SLAM, and its repository is written in Python.
sentences.note: Description gives Visual Inertial Gaussian Splatting SLAM; language is Python.

sentences.text: The main technical risk is that results shown in papers may not hold on messy field data, and the evidence has no benchmarks or deployment results to judge this.
The VidMap abstract says accurately recovering camera calibration and metric poses for any unconstrained video would unlock large-scale training data for navigation and scene understanding.
sentences.note: Abstract says recovering calibration and metric poses would unlock the data, not just accurate poses.

sentences.text: If that holds, the buyer could be robotics teams that need labeled motion data from ordinary video.
The evidence contains no market sizing, customer, or pricing information, so this is only a hypothesis.
